accuracy.evidence: Matches KS1 past animals / fossil evidence: dinosaurs real, lived millions of years before people; fossils = bones/teeth/footprints/eggs in rock; toys and dragons are not evidence.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets toy=real, dragon=dinosaur, people-with-dinos, all-huge, and non-rock 'fossils' in predictions, sort, mix, challenge why(), and adult notes.

lab_distinct.evidence: Lab is deep-time placement plus fossil-vs-toy sorting for dinosaurs — distinct from how-fossils-form sequence (flagfoss) and from mammal traits (flagwhale).

lab_teaches.evidence: Learner must place dinosaurs before people, dig four fossil clues, sort evidence from toys, match a tooth to meat-eater, and show big and small before confirmation text.

predictions.evidence: Wrong options (people first; plastic toy as fossil; all dinosaurs huge; cartoons as proof) are overturned by later tasks.

challenge_feedback.evidence: why() names toy/shop, dragon/cartoon, people-together, paint/coin, and size slips specifically.

readability.evidence: Ages 5–7 wording: short kid lines, concrete bone/tooth/footprint examples, fossil defined in-lab.

no_filler.evidence: No delve/journey phrasing; each line teaches deep time, fossil evidence, or a myth to reject.

mobile.evidence: Large timeline and sort buttons; dig taps and challenge stack work at phone width.

accessibility.evidence: Timeline, dig, sort, match, and size steps expose lbtn twins; say() updates canvas aria-label; challenge uses aria-live status.

sources: UK National Curriculum 2013 Science KS1: Animals including humans; Working scientifically — using evidence
